item.title: Being a prepper once came with a stigma. Recent outages are turning skeptics into believers
item.description: In the wake of a series of tech failures, major government network crashes and flight stoppages, many people online are looking to preppers to learn how to become self-reliant.
item.content:encoded: In the wake of a series of tech failures, major government network crashes and flight stoppages, many people online are looking to preppers to learn how to become self-reliant.

item.title: At Albuquerque's Indian Pueblo Kitchen, Native American dishes are the main course
item.description: At an Albuquerque, N.M., museum, the restaurant is just as much of a draw as the exhibitions, with dishes like green chile stew and sweet biscochitos flavored with anise and cinnamon.

item.title: Powerful storms disrupt holiday travel, as Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade is postponed
item.description: Extreme weather that has unleashed strong winds, high tides, heavy rain and floods is expected to impact travel plans of an estimated 81.5 million people as they travel across the United States.

item.title: Severe weather took a toll on Wisconsin's cranberry production this year
item.description: Wisconsin grows more cranberries than any other state, supplying much of the fruit Americans enjoy at Thanksgiving. But some of the state's growers are reporting disappointing harvests this fall, following a season of challenging weather.

item.title: U.S. Judge rules FCC violated ABC's free speech rights to please Trump
item.description: A federal judge has blocked the Trump administration from moving to review all local broadcast licenses held by ABC. The stations air in six of the largest U.S. markets.

item.title: In a flash, the Army blew up nearly 5 tons of a degraded explosive at its plant in Iowa
item.description: The controlled detonation of more than 60 barrels of unstable lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown is complete. The explosive had been stored at the plant for nearly 20 years.

item.title: In a time of rising costs, one Thanksgiving commodity is cheaper: cannabis
